types.description: The product accepts path input in the form of asterisk wildcard ('filedir*') without appropriate validation, which can lead to ambiguous path resolution and allow an attacker to traverse the file system to unintended locations or access arbitrary files.

types.name: Use of umask() with chmod-style Argument
types.description: The product calls umask() with an incorrect argument that is specified as if it is an argument to chmod().

types.name: Dead Code
types.description: The product contains dead code, which can never be executed.

types.name: Return of Stack Variable Address
types.description: A function returns the address of a stack variable.

types.name: Assignment to Variable without Use
types.description: The variable's value is assigned but never used, i.e., is a dead store. That is, after the assignment, the variable is either assigned another value or goes out of scope.

types.name: Use of Hibernate with HQL/SQL Query String Containing External Input
types.description: The product uses Hibernate to execute a dynamic HQL or SQL statement, but the statement is built with user-controlled input.

types.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking
types.description: The product relies on the existence or values of cookies when performing security-critical operations, but it does not properly ensure that the setting is valid for the associated user.

types.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled SQL Primary Key
types.description: The product uses a database table that includes records that should not be accessible to an actor, but it executes a SQL statement with a primary key that can be controlled by that actor.

types.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
types.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

types.name: finalize() Method Without super.finalize()
types.description: The product contains a finalize() method that does not call super.finalize().

types.name: Path Equivalence: 'fakedir/../realdir/filename'
types.description: The product contains protection mechanisms to restrict access to 'realdir/filename', but it constructs pathnames using external input in the form of 'fakedir/../realdir/filename' that are not handled by those mechanisms. This allows attackers to perform unauthorized actions against the targeted file.

types.name: Expression is Always False
types.description: The product contains an expression that will always evaluate to false.

types.name: Expression is Always True
types.description: The product contains an expression that will always evaluate to true.

types.name: Call to Thread run() instead of start()
types.description: The product calls a thread's run() method instead of calling start().

types.name: Improper Following of Specification by Caller
types.description: The product does not follow or incorrectly follows the specifications as required by the implementation language, environment, framework, protocol, or platform.

types.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Synchronization Primitives
types.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using thread synchronization primitives.

types.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of AWT Swing
types.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using AWT/Swing.

types.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Java I/O
types.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using the java.io package.

types.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Sockets
types.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using sockets.

types.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Class Loader
types.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using the class loader.

types.name: J2EE Bad Practices: Non-serializable Object Stored in Session
types.description: The product stores a non-serializable object as an HttpSession attribute.

types.name: Path Equivalence: Windows 8.3 Filename
types.description: The product contains a protection mechanism that restricts access to a long filename on a Windows operating system, but it does not properly restrict access to the equivalent short "8.3" filename.

types.name: clone() Method Without super.clone()
types.description: The product contains a clone() method that does not call super.clone() to obtain the new object.

types.name: Object Model Violation: Just One of Equals and Hashcode Defined
types.description: The product does not maintain equal hashcodes for equal objects.

types.name: Array Declared Public, Final, and Static
types.description: The product declares an array public, final, and static, which is not sufficient to prevent the array's contents from being modified.

types.name: finalize() Method Declared Public
types.description: The product violates secure coding principles for mobile code by declaring a finalize() method public.

types.name: Return Inside Finally Block
types.description: The code has a return statement inside a finally block.

types.name: Empty Synchronized Block
types.description: The product contains an empty synchronized block.

types.name: Explicit Call to Finalize()
types.description: The product makes an explicit call to the finalize() method from outside the finalizer.

types.name: Assignment of a Fixed Address to a Pointer
types.description: The product sets a pointer to a specific address other than NULL or 0.

types.name: Attempt to Access Child of a Non-structure Pointer
types.description: The product casts a non-structure type to a structure type, then accesses a field within the structure.

types.name: Call to Non-ubiquitous API
types.description: The product uses an API function that does not exist on all versions of the target platform.

types.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access
types.description: The product attempts to access a file based on the filename, but it does not properly prevent that filename from identifying a link or shortcut that resolves to an unintended resource.

types.name: Free of Memory not on the Heap
types.description: The product calls free() on a pointer to memory that was not allocated using associated heap allocation functions such as malloc(), calloc(), or realloc().

types.name: Sensitive Data Storage in Improperly Locked Memory
types.description: The product stores sensitive data in memory that is not locked, or that has been incorrectly locked.

types.name: DEPRECATED: Authentication Bypass Issues
types.description: This weakness has been deprecated because it covered redundant concepts already described in CWE-287.

types.name: Authentication Bypass: OpenSSL CTX Object Modified after SSL Objects are Created
types.description: The product modifies the SSL context after connection creation has begun.

types.name: J2EE Framework: Saving Unserializable Objects to Disk
types.description: The J2EE container attempts to write unserializable objects to disk.

types.name: Comparison of Object References Instead of Object Contents
types.description: The product compares object references instead of the contents of the objects themselves, preventing it from detecting equivalent objects.

types.name: DEPRECATED: Incorrect Semantic Object Comparison
types.description: This weakness has been deprecated. It was poorly described and difficult to distinguish from other entries. It was also inappropriate to assign a separate ID solely because of domain-specific considerations. Its closest equivalent is CWE-1023.

types.name: Use of Wrong Operator in String Comparison
types.description: The product uses the wrong operator when comparing a string, such as using "==" when the .equals() method should be used instead.

types.name: Use of HTTP Request With Sensitive Query String
types.description: The web application uses an HTTP method to process a request, but the request includes sensitive information in the query string.

types.name: Missing Validation of OpenSSL Certificate
types.description: The product uses OpenSSL and trusts or uses a certificate without using the SSL_get_verify_result() function to ensure that the certificate satisfies all necessary security requirements.

types.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Insufficient Session-ID Length
types.description: The J2EE application is configured to use an insufficient session ID length.

types.name: Uncaught Exception in Servlet
types.description: The Servlet does not catch all exceptions.

types.name: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security
types.description: The product includes a server that relies on the client to implement a protection mechanism that is intended to protect the server.

types.name: Use of Client-Side Authentication
types.description: A client/server product performs authentication within client code but not in server code, allowing server-side authentication to be bypassed via a modified client that omits the authentication check.

types.name: Multiple Binds to the Same Port
types.description: When multiple sockets are allowed to bind to the same port, other services on that port may be stolen or spoofed.

types.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
types.description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

types.name: Public Static Final Field References Mutable Object
types.description: A public or protected static final field references a mutable object, which allows the object to be changed by malicious code, or accidentally from another package.

types.name: Struts: Non-private Field in ActionForm Class
types.description: The product uses an ActionForm class that contains a field that has not been declared private.

types.name: Double-Checked Locking
types.description: The product uses double-checked locking to access a resource without the overhead of explicit synchronization, but the locking is insufficient.

types.name: UNIX Symbolic Link (Symlink) Following
types.description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently account for when the file is a symbolic link that resolves to a target outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

types.name: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere
types.description: The product uses an externally controlled name or reference that resolves to a resource that is outside of the intended control sphere.

types.name: Improper Authorization of Index Containing Sensitive Information
types.description: The product creates a search index of private or sensitive documents, but it does not properly limit index access to actors who are authorized to see the original information.

types.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code Comments
types.description: The product's source code includes comments that contain sensitive information, such as filenames related to the application, old links or links that were not meant to be browsed by users, old code fragments, etc.

types.name: Incomplete Identification of Uploaded File Variables (PHP)
types.description: The PHP application uses an old method for processing uploaded files by referencing the four global variables that are set for each file (e.g. $varname, $varname_size, $varname_name, $varname_type).

types.name: Reachable Assertion
types.description: The product contains an assert() or similar statement that can be triggered by an attacker, which leads to an application exit or other behavior that is more severe than necessary.

types.name: Exposed Unsafe ActiveX Method
types.description: An ActiveX control is intended for use in a web browser, but it exposes dangerous methods that perform actions that are outside of the browser's security model (e.g. the zone or domain).

types.name: Dangling Database Cursor
types.description: The product does not close a database cursor properly, leaving the cursor "dangling."

types.name: UNIX Hard Link
types.description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently account for when the name is associated with a hard link to a target that is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

types.name: Unverified Password Change
types.description: When setting a new password for a user, the product does not require knowledge of the original password, or using another form of authentication.

types.name: Variable Extraction Error
types.description: The product uses external input to determine the names of variables into which information is extracted, without verifying that the names of the specified variables are valid.

types.name: Improper Validation of Function Hook Arguments
types.description: The product adds hooks to user-accessible API functions, but it does not properly validate the arguments.

types.name: Unsafe ActiveX Control Marked Safe For Scripting
types.description: The product includes an ActiveX control that is intended for restricted use, but the control has been marked as safe-for-scripting.

types.name: Executable Regular Expression Error
types.description: The product uses a regular expression that either (1) contains an executable component with user-controlled inputs, or (2) allows a user to enable execution by inserting pattern modifiers.

types.name: Permissive Regular Expression
types.description: The product uses a regular expression that does not sufficiently restrict the set of allowed values.

types.name: Null Byte Interaction Error (Poison Null Byte)
types.description: The product does not properly handle null bytes or NUL characters when passing data between different representations or components.

types.name: Dynamic Variable Evaluation
types.description: In a language where the user can influence the name of a variable at runtime, if the variable names are not controlled, an attacker can read or write to arbitrary variables, or access arbitrary functions.

types.name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
types.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine with arguments that are not correctly specified.

types.name: Not Failing Securely
types.description: When the product encounters an error condition or failure, its design requires it to fall back to a state that is less secure than other options that are available, such as selecting the weakest encryption algorithm or using the most permissive access control restrictions.

types.name: Unnecessary Complexity in Protection Mechanism (Not Using 'Economy of Mechanism')
types.description: The product uses a more complex mechanism than necessary, which could lead to resultant weaknesses when the mechanism is not correctly understood, modeled, configured, implemented, or used.

types.name: Not Using Complete Mediation
types.description: The product does not perform access checks on a resource every time the resource is accessed by an entity, which can create resultant weaknesses if that entity's rights or privileges change over time.

types.name: Windows Shortcut Following (.LNK)
types.description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently handle when the file is a Windows shortcut (.LNK) whose target is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

types.name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
types.description: The product contains a mechanism for users to recover or change their passwords without knowing the original password, but the mechanism is weak.

types.name: Improper Restriction of Names for Files and Other Resources
types.description: The product constructs the name of a file or other resource using input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the resulting name.

types.name: External Control of Critical State Data
types.description: The product stores security-critical state information about its users, or the product itself, in a location that is accessible to unauthorized actors.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions
types.description: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XPath expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax
types.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes web scripting syntax in HTTP headers that can be used by web browser components that can process raw headers, such as Flash.

types.name: Overly Restrictive Account Lockout Mechanism
types.description: The product contains an account lockout protection mechanism, but the mechanism is too restrictive and can be triggered too easily, which allows attackers to deny service to legitimate users by causing their accounts to be locked out.

types.name: Reliance on File Name or Extension of Externally-Supplied File
types.description: The product allows a file to be uploaded, but it relies on the file name or extension of the file to determine the appropriate behaviors.

types.name: Use of Non-Canonical URL Paths for Authorization Decisions
types.description: The product defines policy namespaces and makes authorization decisions based on the assumption that a URL is canonical.

types.name: Incorrect Use of Privileged APIs
types.description: The product does not conform to the API requirements for a function call that requires extra privileges. This could allow attackers to gain privileges by causing the function to be called incorrectly.

types.name: Reliance on Obfuscation or Encryption of Security-Relevant Inputs without Integrity Checking
types.description: The product uses obfuscation or encryption of inputs that should not be mutable by an external actor, but the product does not use integrity checks to detect if those inputs have been modified.

types.name: Windows Hard Link
types.description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently handle when the name is associated with a hard link to a target that is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

types.name: Trusting HTTP Permission Methods on the Server Side
types.description: The server contains a protection mechanism that assumes that any URI that is accessed using HTTP GET will not cause a state change to the associated resource.

types.name: Exposure of WSDL File Containing Sensitive Information
types.description: The Web services architecture may require exposing a Web Service Definition Language (WSDL) file that contains information on the publicly accessible services and how callers of these services should interact with them (e.g. what parameters they expect and what types they return).

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions
types.description: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XQuery expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input.

types.name: Improper Isolation or Compartmentalization
types.description: The product does not properly compartmentalize or isolate functionality, processes, or resources that require different privilege levels, rights, or permissions.

types.name: Reliance on a Single Factor in a Security Decision
types.description: A protection mechanism relies exclusively, or to a large extent, on the evaluation of a single condition or the integrity of a single object or entity in order to make a decision about granting access to restricted resources or functionality.

types.name: Insufficient Psychological Acceptability
types.description: The product has a protection mechanism that is too difficult or inconvenient to use, encouraging non-malicious users to disable or bypass the mechanism, whether by accident or on purpose.

types.name: Reliance on Security Through Obscurity
types.description: The product uses a protection mechanism whose strength depends heavily on its obscurity, such that knowledge of its algorithms or key data is sufficient to defeat the mechanism.
aliases: Never Assuming your secrets are safe

types.name: Violation of Secure Design Principles
types.description: The product violates well-established principles for secure design.

types.name: Improper Handling of File Names that Identify Virtual Resources
types.description: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles a file name that identifies a "virtual" resource that is not directly specified within the directory that is associated with the file name.

types.name: Improper Synchronization
types.description: The product utilizes multiple threads, processes, components, or systems to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

types.name: Use of a Non-reentrant Function in a Concurrent Context
types.description: The product calls a non-reentrant function in a concurrent context in which a competing code sequence (e.g. thread or signal handler) may have an opportunity to call the same function or otherwise influence its state.

types.name: Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime
types.description: The product does not maintain or incorrectly maintains control over a resource throughout its lifetime of creation, use, and release.

types.name: Improper Initialization
types.description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource.

types.name: Operation on Resource in Wrong Phase of Lifetime
types.description: The product performs an operation on a resource at the wrong phase of the resource's lifecycle, which can lead to unexpected behaviors.

types.name: Improper Locking
types.description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

types.name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
types.description: The product exposes a resource to the wrong control sphere, providing unintended actors with inappropriate access to the resource.

types.name: Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres
types.description: The product does not properly transfer a resource/behavior to another sphere, or improperly imports a resource/behavior from another sphere, in a manner that provides unintended control over that resource.

types.name: Improper Handling of Windows Device Names
types.description: The product constructs pathnames from user input, but it does not handle or incorrectly handles a pathname containing a Windows device name such as AUX or CON. This typically leads to denial of service or an information exposure when the application attempts to process the pathname as a regular file.

types.name: Always-Incorrect Control Flow Implementation
types.description: The code contains a control flow path that does not reflect the algorithm that the path is intended to implement, leading to incorrect behavior any time this path is navigated.

types.name: Lack of Administrator Control over Security
types.description: The product uses security features in a way that prevents the product's administrator from tailoring security settings to reflect the environment in which the product is being used.

types.name: Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release
types.description: The product uses, accesses, or otherwise operates on a resource after that resource has been expired, released, or revoked.

types.name: External Influence of Sphere Definition
types.description: The product does not prevent the definition of control spheres from external actors.

types.name: Uncontrolled Recursion
types.description: The product does not properly control the amount of recursion that takes place, consuming excessive resources, such as allocated memory or the program stack.

types.name: Multiple Operations on Resource in Single-Operation Context
types.description: The product performs the same operation on a resource two or more times, when the operation should only be applied once.

types.name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
types.description: The product invokes a potentially dangerous function that could introduce a vulnerability if it is used incorrectly, but the function can also be used safely.

types.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Overflow
types.description: The product performs a calculation to determine how much memory to allocate, but an integer overflow can occur that causes less memory to be allocated than expected, leading to a buffer overflow.

types.name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
types.description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.

types.name: Incorrect Calculation
types.description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.

types.name: Function Call With Incorrect Order of Arguments
types.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies the arguments in an incorrect order.

types.name: Incorrect Provision of Specified Functionality
types.description: The code does not function according to its published specifications, potentially leading to incorrect usage.

types.name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
types.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies too many arguments, or too few arguments, which may lead to undefined behavior and resultant weaknesses.

types.name: Function Call With Incorrect Argument Type
types.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies an argument that is the wrong data type, which may lead to resultant weaknesses.

types.name: Function Call With Incorrectly Specified Argument Value
types.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies an argument that contains the wrong value, which may lead to resultant weaknesses.

types.name: Function Call With Incorrect Variable or Reference as Argument
types.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies the wrong variable or reference as one of the arguments, which may lead to undefined behavior and resultant weaknesses.

types.name: Permission Race Condition During Resource Copy
types.description: The product, while copying or cloning a resource, does not set the resource's permissions or access control until the copy is complete, leaving the resource exposed to other spheres while the copy is taking place.

types.name: Improper Handling of Windows ::DATA Alternate Data Stream
types.description: The product does not properly prevent access to, or detect usage of, alternate data streams (ADS).

types.name: Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference
types.description: The product does not check for an error after calling a function that can return with a NULL pointer if the function fails, which leads to a resultant NULL pointer dereference.

types.name: Insufficient Control Flow Management
types.description: The code does not sufficiently manage its control flow during execution, creating conditions in which the control flow can be modified in unexpected ways.

types.name: Incomplete Denylist to Cross-Site Scripting
types.description: The product uses a denylist-based protection mechanism to defend against XSS attacks, but the denylist is incomplete.

types.name: Protection Mechanism Failure
types.description: The product does not use or incorrectly uses a protection mechanism that provides sufficient defense against directed attacks against the product.

types.name: Use of Multiple Resources with Duplicate Identifier
types.description: The product uses multiple resources that can have the same identifier, in a context in which unique identifiers are required.

types.name: Use of Low-Level Functionality
types.description: The product uses low-level functionality that is explicitly prohibited by the framework or specification under which the product is supposed to operate.

types.name: Incorrect Behavior Order
types.description: The product performs multiple related behaviors, but the behaviors are performed in the wrong order in ways that may produce resultant weaknesses.

types.name: Incorrect Comparison
types.description: The product compares two entities in a security-relevant context, but the comparison is incorrect.

types.name: Execution After Redirect (EAR)
types.description: The web application sends a redirect to another location, but instead of exiting, it executes additional code.

types.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Missing Custom Error Page
types.description: The product has a J2EE component that does not have a custom error page.

types.name: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
types.description: The product does not properly anticipate or handle exceptional conditions that rarely occur during normal operation of the product.

types.name: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
types.description: The product does not correctly convert an object, resource, or structure from one type to a different type.

types.name: Incorrect Control Flow Scoping
types.description: The product does not properly return control flow to the proper location after it has completed a task or detected an unusual condition.

types.name: Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference
types.description: The product uses a name or reference to access a resource, but the name/reference resolves to a resource that is outside of the intended control sphere.

types.name: Improper Neutralization
types.description: The product does not ensure or incorrectly ensures that structured messages or data are well-formed and that certain security properties are met before being used when received from an upstream component, or before being sent to a downstream component.

types.name: Incorrect Ownership Assignment
types.description: The product assigns an owner to a resource, but the owner is outside of the intended control sphere.

types.name: DEPRECATED: Apple '.DS_Store'
types.description: This entry has been deprecated as it represents a specific observed example of a UNIX Hard Link weakness type rather than its own individual weakness type. Please refer to CWE-62.

types.name: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
types.description: The product does not follow certain coding rules for development.

types.name: Improper Handling of Apple HFS+ Alternate Data Stream Path
types.description: The product does not properly handle special paths that may identify the data or resource fork of a file on the HFS+ file system.

types.name: External Control of File Name or Path
types.description: The product allows user input to control or influence paths or file names that are used in filesystem operations.

types.name: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code
types.description: The developer builds a security-critical protection mechanism into the software, but the compiler optimizes the program such that the mechanism is removed or modified.

types.name: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
types.description: The product provides an Applications Programming Interface (API) or similar interface for interaction with external actors, but the interface includes a dangerous method or function that is not properly restricted.

types.name: Failure to Sanitize Special Elements into a Different Plane
types.description: The product does not adequately filter user-controlled input for special elements with control implications.

types.name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
types.description: The product does not check or incorrectly checks for unusual or exceptional conditions that are not expected to occur frequently during day to day operation of the product.

types.name: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
types.description: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles an exceptional condition.

types.name: Missing Custom Error Page
types.description: The product does not return custom error pages to the user, possibly exposing sensitive information.

types.name: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation
types.description: A protocol or its implementation supports interaction between multiple actors and allows those actors to negotiate which algorithm should be used in a protection mechanism such as encryption or authentication, but it does not select the strongest algorithm that is available to both parties.

types.name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
types.description: The product uses an API function, data structure, or other entity in a way that relies on properties that are not always guaranteed to hold for that entity.

types.name: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt
types.description: The product uses a one-way cryptographic hash against an input that should not be reversible, such as a password, but the product does not also use a salt as part of the input.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Equivalent Special Elements
types.description: The product correctly neutralizes certain special elements, but it improperly neutralizes equivalent special elements.

types.name: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt
types.description: The product uses a one-way cryptographic hash against an input that should not be reversible, such as a password, but the product uses a predictable salt as part of the input.

types.name: Free of Pointer not at Start of Buffer
types.description: The product calls free() on a pointer to a memory resource that was allocated on the heap, but the pointer is not at the start of the buffer.

types.name: Mismatched Memory Management Routines
types.description: The product attempts to return a memory resource to the system, but it calls a release function that is not compatible with the function that was originally used to allocate that resource.

types.name: Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference
types.description: The product attempts to return a memory resource to the system, but it calls the wrong release function or calls the appropriate release function incorrectly.

types.name: Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource
types.description: The product locks a critical resource more times than intended, leading to an unexpected state in the system.

types.name: Multiple Unlocks of a Critical Resource
types.description: The product unlocks a critical resource more times than intended, leading to an unexpected state in the system.

types.name: Critical Data Element Declared Public
types.description: The product declares a critical variable, field, or member to be public when intended security policy requires it to be private.

types.name: Access to Critical Private Variable via Public Method
types.description: The product defines a public method that reads or modifies a private variable.

types.name: Incorrect Short Circuit Evaluation
types.description: The product contains a conditional statement with multiple logical expressions in which one of the non-leading expressions may produce side effects.

types.name: DEPRECATED: Uncontrolled File Descriptor Consumption
types.description: This entry has been deprecated because it was a duplicate of CWE-774. All content has been transferred to CWE-774.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command
types.description: The product constructs all or part of a command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended command when it is sent to a downstream component.

types.name: Missing Reference to Active Allocated Resource
types.description: The product does not properly maintain a reference to a resource that has been allocated, which prevents the resource from being reclaimed.

types.name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
types.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

types.name: Missing Reference to Active File Descriptor or Handle
types.description: The product does not properly maintain references to a file descriptor or handle, which prevents that file descriptor/handle from being reclaimed.

types.name: Allocation of File Descriptors or Handles Without Limits or Throttling
types.description: The product allocates file descriptors or handles on behalf of an actor without imposing any restrictions on how many descriptors can be allocated, in violation of the intended security policy for that actor.

types.name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
types.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

types.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs
types.description: The product uses XML documents and allows their structure to be defined with a Document Type Definition (DTD), but it does not properly control the number of recursive definitions of entities.

types.name: Regular Expression without Anchors
types.description: The product uses a regular expression to perform neutralization, but the regular expression omits one or more anchors that may allow malicious or malformed data to slip through.

types.name: Insufficient Logging
types.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

types.name: Logging of Excessive Data
types.description: The product logs too much information, making log files hard to process and possibly hindering recovery efforts or forensic analysis after an attack.

types.name: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP
types.description: The product uses the RSA algorithm but does not incorporate Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding (OAEP).

types.name: Improper Address Validation in IOCTL with METHOD_NEITHER I/O Control Code
types.description: The product defines an IOCTL that uses METHOD_NEITHER for I/O, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates the addresses that are provided.

types.name: Exposed IOCTL with Insufficient Access Control
types.description: The product implements an IOCTL with functionality that should be restricted, but it does not properly enforce access control for the IOCTL.

types.name: Operator Precedence Logic Error
types.description: The product uses an expression in which operator precedence causes incorrect logic to be used.

types.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking in a Security Decision
types.description: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of a cookie, but it does not properly ensure that the cookie is valid for the associated user.

types.name: Use of Path Manipulation Function without Maximum-sized Buffer
types.description: The product invokes a function for normalizing paths or file names, but it provides an output buffer that is smaller than the maximum possible size, such as PATH_MAX.

types.name: Access of Memory Location Before Start of Buffer
types.description: The product reads or writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location prior to the beginning of the buffer.

types.name: Access of Memory Location After End of Buffer
types.description: The product reads or writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location after the end of the buffer.

types.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
types.description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.

types.name: Improper Filtering of Special Elements
types.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but it does not filter or incorrectly filters special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

types.name: Incomplete Filtering of Special Elements
types.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but it does not completely filter special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

types.name: Incomplete Filtering of One or More Instances of Special Elements
types.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not completely filter one or more instances of special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

types.name: Only Filtering One Instance of a Special Element
types.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only filters a single instance of a special element before sending it to a downstream component.

types.name: Incomplete Filtering of Multiple Instances of Special Elements
types.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but it does not filter all instances of a special element before sending it to a downstream component.

types.name: Only Filtering Special Elements at a Specified Location
types.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements at a specified location, thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

types.name: Only Filtering Special Elements Relative to a Marker
types.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements positioned relative to a marker (e.g. "at the beginning/end of a string; the second argument"), thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

types.name: Only Filtering Special Elements at an Absolute Position
types.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements at an absolute position (e.g. "byte number 10"), thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

types.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Entity Bean Declared Remote
types.description: The J2EE application exposes a remote interface for an entity bean, but it also exposes methods that get or set the bean's data.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page
types.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special characters such as "", and "&" that could be interpreted as web-scripting elements when they are sent to a downstream component that processes web pages.

types.name: Guessable CAPTCHA
types.description: The product uses a CAPTCHA challenge, but the challenge can be guessed or automatically recognized by a non-human actor.

types.name: Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value
types.description: The product uses a sequential operation to read or write a buffer, but it uses an incorrect length value that causes it to access memory that is outside of the bounds of the buffer.

types.name: Buffer Access Using Size of Source Buffer
types.description: The product uses the size of a source buffer when reading from or writing to a destination buffer, which may cause it to access memory that is outside of the bounds of the buffer.

types.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
types.description: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of an input, but the input can be modified by an untrusted actor in a way that bypasses the protection mechanism.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in an Error Message Web Page
types.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special characters that could be interpreted as web-scripting elements when they are sent to an error page.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes of IMG Tags in a Web Page
types.description: The web application does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes scripting elements within attributes of HTML IMG tags, such as the src attribute.

types.name: Missing Synchronization
types.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

types.name: Incorrect Synchronization
types.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.

types.name: Untrusted Pointer Dereference
types.description: The product obtains a value from an untrusted source, converts this value to a pointer, and dereferences the resulting pointer.

types.name: Use of Out-of-range Pointer Offset
types.description: The product performs pointer arithmetic on a valid pointer, but it uses an offset that can point outside of the intended range of valid memory locations for the resulting pointer.

types.name: Access of Uninitialized Pointer
types.description: The product accesses or uses a pointer that has not been initialized.

types.name: Expired Pointer Dereference
types.description: The product dereferences a pointer that contains a location for memory that was previously valid, but is no longer valid.

types.name: Premature Release of Resource During Expected Lifetime
types.description: The product releases a resource that is still intended to be used by itself or another actor.

types.name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
types.description: The product does not restrict a reference to a Document Type Definition (DTD) to the intended control sphere. This might allow attackers to reference arbitrary DTDs, possibly causing the product to expose files, consume excessive system resources, or execute arbitrary http requests on behalf of the attacker.

types.name: Signal Handler with Functionality that is not Asynchronous-Safe
types.description: The product defines a signal handler that contains code sequences that are not asynchronous-safe, i.e., the functionality is not reentrant, or it can be interrupted.

types.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
types.description: The product imports, requires, or includes executable functionality (such as a library) from a source that is outside of the intended control sphere.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes in a Web Page
types.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes "javascript:" or other URIs from dangerous attributes within tags, such as onmouseover, onload, onerror, or style.

types.name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
types.description: The product includes web functionality (such as a web widget) from another domain in a way that causes the functionality to operate within the domain of the product, potentially granting total access and control of the product to the untrusted source.

types.name: Signal Handler Function Associated with Multiple Signals
types.description: The product defines a function that is used as a handler for more than one signal.

types.name: Unlock of a Resource that is not Locked
types.description: The product attempts to unlock a resource that is not locked.

types.name: Deadlock
types.description: The product contains multiple threads or executable segments that are waiting for each other to release a necessary lock, resulting in deadlock.

types.name: Excessive Iteration
types.description: The product performs an iteration or loop without sufficiently limiting the number of times that the loop is executed.

types.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition
types.description: The product contains an iteration or loop with an exit condition that cannot be reached, i.e., an infinite loop.

types.name: Use of Password Hash Instead of Password for Authentication
types.description: The product includes a client that computes a hash of a password and sends the hash to another component, which compares the supplied hash to the hash obtained from a data store of password hashes.

types.name: Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action
types.description: The product requires that an actor should only be able to perform an action once, or to have only one unique action, but the product does not enforce or incorrectly enforces this restriction.

types.name: Inappropriate Encoding for Output Context
types.description: The product uses or specifies an encoding when generating output to a downstream component, but the specified encoding is not the same as the encoding that is expected by the downstream component.

types.name: Numeric Range Comparison Without Minimum Check
types.description: The product checks a value to ensure that it is less than or equal to a maximum, but it does not also verify that the value is greater than or equal to the minimum.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Encoded URI Schemes in a Web Page
types.description: The web application improperly neutralizes user-controlled input for executable script disguised with URI encodings.

types.name: Placement of User into Incorrect Group
types.description: The product or the administrator places a user into an incorrect group.

types.name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type
types.description: The product allocates or initializes a resource such as a pointer, object, or variable using one type, but it later accesses that resource using a type that is incompatible with the original type.

types.name: Doubled Character XSS Manipulations
types.description: The web application does not filter user-controlled input for executable script disguised using doubling of the involved characters.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Invalid Characters in Identifiers in Web Pages
types.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes invalid characters or byte sequences in the middle of tag names, URI schemes, and other identifiers.

types.name: Incorrect Authorization
types.description: The product performs an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action, but it does not correctly perform the check.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Alternate XSS Syntax
types.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controlled input for alternate script syntax.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command
types.description: The product constructs a string for a command to be executed by a separate component in another control sphere, but it does not properly delimit the intended arguments, options, or switches within that command string.

types.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Weak Access Permissions for EJB Methods
types.description: If elevated access rights are assigned to EJB methods, then an attacker can take advantage of the permissions to exploit the product.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query
types.description: The product constructs all or part of an LDAP query using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended LDAP query when it is sent to a downstream component.

types.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource
types.description: The product uses or accesses a resource that has not been initialized.

types.name: Missing Initialization of Resource
types.description: The product does not initialize a critical resource.

types.name: XML Injection
types.description: The product does not properly neutralize special elements that are used in XML, allowing attackers to modify the syntax, content, or commands of the XML before it is processed by an end system.

types.name: Use of Expired File Descriptor
types.description: The product uses or accesses a file descriptor after it has been closed.

types.name: Improper Update of Reference Count
types.description: The product uses a reference count to manage a resource, but it does not update or incorrectly updates the reference count.

types.name: Hidden Functionality
types.description: The product contains functionality that is not documented, not part of the specification, and not accessible through an interface or command sequence that is obvious to the product's users or administrators.

types.name: Improper Control of Dynamically-Managed Code Resources
types.description: The product does not properly restrict reading from or writing to dynamically-managed code resources such as variables, objects, classes, attributes, functions, or executable instructions or statements.

types.name: Improper Control of Dynamically-Identified Variables
types.description: The product does not properly restrict reading from or writing to dynamically-identified variables.

types.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
types.description: The product generates a hash for a password, but it uses a scheme that does not provide a sufficient level of computational effort that would make password cracking attacks infeasible or expensive.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement
types.description: The product constructs all or part of an expression language (EL) statement in a framework such as a Java Server Page (JSP) using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended EL statement before it is executed.

types.name: DEPRECATED: Improper Sanitization of Custom Special Characters
types.description: This entry has been deprecated. It originally came from PLOVER, which sometimes defined "other" and "miscellaneous" categories in order to satisfy exhaustiveness requirements for taxonomies. Within the context of CWE, the use of a more abstract entry is preferred in mapping situations. CWE-75 is a more appropriate mapping.

types.name: Improper Restriction of Power Consumption
types.description: The product operates in an environment in which power is a limited resource that cannot be automatically replenished - or has financial restrictions - but the product does not properly restrict the amount of power that its operation consumes.

types.name: Storage of Sensitive Data in a Mechanism without Access Control
types.description: The product stores sensitive information in a file system or device that does not have built-in access control.

types.name: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
types.description: The product stores sensitive information without properly limiting read or write access by unauthorized actors.

types.name: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
types.description: The product establishes a communication channel to (or from) an endpoint for privileged or protected operations, but it does not properly ensure that it is communicating with the correct endpoint.

types.name: Improper Enforcement of Message Integrity During Transmission in a Communication Channel
types.description: The product establishes a communication channel with an endpoint and receives a message from that endpoint, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the message was not modified during transmission.

types.name: Improper Verification of Intent by Broadcast Receiver
types.description: The Android application uses a Broadcast Receiver that receives an Intent but does not properly verify that the Intent came from an authorized source.

types.name: Improper Export of Android Application Components
types.description: The Android application exports a component for use by other applications, but does not properly restrict which applications can launch the component or access the data it contains.

types.name: Use of Implicit Intent for Sensitive Communication
types.description: The Android application uses an implicit intent for transmitting sensitive data to other applications.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences
types.description: The product uses CRLF (carriage return line feeds) as a special element, e.g. to separate lines or records, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes CRLF sequences from inputs.

types.name: Improper Authorization in Handler for Custom URL Scheme
types.description: The product uses a handler for a custom URL scheme, but it does not properly restrict which actors can invoke the handler using the scheme.

types.name: Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel
types.description: The product establishes a communication channel to handle an incoming request that has been initiated by an actor, but it does not properly verify that the request is coming from the expected origin.

types.name: Incorrectly Specified Destination in a Communication Channel
types.description: The product creates a communication channel to initiate an outgoing request to an actor, but it does not correctly specify the intended destination for that actor.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
types.description: The product generates a query intended to access or manipulate data in a data store such as a database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that can modify the intended logic of the query.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code
types.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes code syntax before using the input in a dynamic evaluation call (e.g. "eval").

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Statically Saved Code
types.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes code syntax before inserting the input into an executable resource, such as a library, configuration file, or template.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Server-Side Includes (SSI) Within a Web Page
types.description: The product generates a web page, but does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input that could be interpreted as a server-side include (SSI) directive.

types.name: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program
types.description: The PHP application receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before its usage in "require," "include," or similar functions.

types.name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers
types.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended control sphere.

types.name: Dangling DNS or deprovisioned service reference
types.description: DNS references a deprovisioned or unavailable external service. Establish impact separately: a dangling record does not by itself demonstrate takeover.

types.name: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
types.description: The product does not sufficiently verify the origin or authenticity of data, in a way that causes it to accept invalid data.

types.name: Excessive agency
types.description: An AI agent has unnecessary capabilities, permissions, or autonomy enabling harmful actions.

types.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
types.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

types.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests
types.description: The product acts as an intermediary HTTP agent (such as a proxy or firewall) in the data flow between two entities such as a client and server, but it does not interpret malformed HTTP requests or responses in ways that are consistent with how the messages will be processed by those entities that are at the ultimate destination.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers
types.description: The product receives data from an HTTP agent/component (e.g., web server, proxy, browser, etc.), but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes CR and LF characters before the data is included in outgoing HTTP headers.

types.name: Insecure direct object reference
types.description: Manipulating an object identifier bypasses object-level access restrictions. Requires an object-reference access-control failure.

types.name: Improper Certificate Validation
types.description: The product does not validate, or incorrectly validates, a certificate.

types.name: Improper Privilege Management
types.description: The product does not properly assign, modify, track, or check privileges for an actor, creating an unintended sphere of control for that actor.

types.name: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
types.description: The product does not verify, or incorrectly verifies, the cryptographic signature for data.

types.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
types.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

types.name: Indirect prompt injection
types.description: Instructions in retrieved documents, tool responses, or other external content redirect an AI system across its intended boundaries.

types.name: Injection
types.description: Untrusted data changes the structure of an interpreted command or query.

types.name: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
types.description: The Secure attribute for sensitive cookies in HTTPS sessions is not set.

types.name: Insecure deserialization
types.description: Untrusted serialized objects trigger unintended behavior during deserialization.

types.name: DEPRECATED: Insufficient Session Expiration
types.description: This entry has been deprecated because it was insufficiently clear. Consider CWE-1462 and its descendants.

types.name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
types.description: The product performs a calculation that can produce an integer overflow or wraparound when the logic assumes that the resulting value will always be larger than the original value. This occurs when an integer value is incremented to a value that is too large to store in the associated representation. When this occurs, the value may become a very small or negative number.

types.name: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
types.description: The product constructs a log message from external input, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements when the message is written to a log file.

types.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
types.description: The product receives input from an upstream component that specifies multiple attributes, properties, or fields that are to be initialized or updated in an object, but it does not properly control which attributes can be modified.

types.name: Missing Authentication for Critical Functionality
types.description: The product does not perform any authentication for functionality that requires a provable user identity or consumes a significant amount of resources.

types.name: Missing authorization
types.description: A sensitive operation lacks a required permission or ownership check. Authentication alone does not establish authorization.

types.name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
types.description: The product uses a cookie to store sensitive information, but the cookie is not marked with the HttpOnly flag.

types.name: Improper Control of Interaction Frequency
types.description: The product does not properly limit the number or frequency of interactions that it has with an actor, such as the number of incoming requests.

types.name: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
types.description: The product does not encrypt sensitive or critical information before storage or transmission.

types.name: Model or training data poisoning
types.description: Attacker-controlled model artifacts or training data change model behavior across an intended integrity boundary.

types.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site
types.description: The web application accepts a user-controlled input that specifies a link to an external site, and uses that link in a redirect.

types.name: Origin Validation Error
types.description: The product does not properly verify that the source of data or communication is valid.

types.name: Out-of-bounds Read
types.description: The product reads data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.

types.name: Out-of-bounds Write
types.description: The product writes data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.

types.name: Path traversal
types.description: Attacker-controlled paths escape an intended filesystem directory.

types.name: Permissive Cross-domain Security Policy with Untrusted Domains
types.description: The product uses a web-client protection mechanism such as a Content Security Policy (CSP) or cross-domain policy file, but the policy includes untrusted domains with which the web client is allowed to communicate.

types.name: Prompt injection
types.description: Attacker-controlled instructions cause an AI system to cross an intended instruction or action boundary.

types.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization
types.description: The product contains a concurrent code sequence that requires temporary, exclusive access to a shared resource, but a timing window exists in which the shared resource can be modified by another code sequence operating concurrently.

types.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
types.description: The product uses a regular expression with a worst-case computational complexity that is inefficient and possibly exponential.

types.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
types.description: The product does not properly control the allocation and maintenance of a limited resource.

types.name: Retrieval, vector or agent memory poisoning
types.description: Attacker-controlled retrieval, embeddings or persistent agent memory alter trusted context or future actions across an intended boundary.

types.name: Security misconfiguration
types.description: An observed configuration defeats an intended security control. A hardening recommendation without an affected security boundary is not sufficient.

types.name: Sensitive data exposure
types.description: Sensitive information is disclosed to an unauthorized recipient.

types.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
types.description: The product writes sensitive information to a log file.

types.name: Session Fixation
types.description: Authenticating a user, or otherwise establishing a new user session, without invalidating any existing session identifier gives an attacker the opportunity to steal authenticated sessions.

types.name: SQL injection
types.description: Attacker-controlled input changes SQL query syntax or meaning. Excludes safely parameterized SQL.

types.name: Server-side request forgery
types.description: Attacker controls server-side network request destinations across an intended trust boundary.

types.name: Stored cross-site scripting
types.description: Attacker input is persisted and later executes as script in another user browser.

types.name: Subdomain takeover
types.description: An attacker can claim the external resource referenced by an organization's DNS and serve content under its hostname. Requires demonstrated claimability or equivalent proof.

types.name: Hidden instruction or system prompt exposure
types.description: Protected system instructions or hidden context cross an intended confidentiality boundary. Public prompt templates alone do not establish impact.

types.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
types.description: The product uses a template engine to insert or process externally-influenced input, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements or syntax that can be interpreted as template expressions or other code directives when processed by the engine.

types.name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
types.description: Two separate operations in a product require different amounts of time to complete, in a way that is observable to an actor and reveals security-relevant information about the state of the product, such as whether a particular operation was successful or not.

types.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
types.description: The product allocates a reusable resource or group of resources on behalf of an actor without imposing any intended restrictions on the size or number of resources that can be allocated.

types.name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
types.description: The product relies on third-party components that are not actively supported or maintained by the original developer or a trusted proxy for the original developer.

types.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
types.description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

types.name: Improper Validation of Generative AI Output
types.description: The product invokes a generative AI/ML component whose behaviors and outputs cannot be directly controlled, but the product does not validate or insufficiently validates the outputs to ensure that they align with the intended security, content, or privacy policy.

types.name: Unsafe reliance on model output
types.description: Unverified model-generated claims drive security-sensitive or consequential decisions without required validation.

types.name: Unsafe tool use
types.description: An AI system invokes tools with unsafe arguments or without required authorization or approval.

types.name: Use After Free
types.description: The product reuses or references memory after it has been freed. At some point afterward, the memory may be allocated again and saved in another pointer, while the original pointer references a location somewhere within the new allocation. Any operations using the original pointer are no longer valid because the memory "belongs" to the code that operates on the new pointer.

types.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
types.description: The product generates an error message that includes sensitive information about its environment, users, or associated data.

types.name: Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component
types.description: The product has a dependency on a third-party component that contains one or more known vulnerabilities.

types.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
types.description: The product uses a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm or protocol.

types.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
types.description: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.

frameworks.coverage: All 984 published weaknesses. Deprecated entries and grouping pillars remain reference records; deprecated choices cannot be assigned.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001
frameworks.coverage: Framework reference only. Licensed Annex A control content is not bundled.

frameworks.name: MITRE ATLAS
frameworks.coverage: Complete tactics, techniques/subtechniques and mitigation index; case studies, software and entities are not choices.

frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-171
frameworks.coverage: Complete publisher OSCAL index, including groups and nested controls/enhancements. Withdrawn entries are marked deprecated. Discovery summaries are not complete control text.

frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-53
frameworks.coverage: Complete publisher OSCAL index, including groups and nested controls/enhancements. Withdrawn entries are marked deprecated. Discovery summaries are not complete control text.

frameworks.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
frameworks.coverage: Complete publisher OSCAL index, including groups and nested controls/enhancements. Withdrawn entries are marked deprecated. Discovery summaries are not complete control text.

frameworks.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
frameworks.coverage: Complete publisher OSCAL index, including groups and nested controls/enhancements. Withdrawn entries are marked deprecated. Discovery summaries are not complete control text.

frameworks.name: NIST Secure Software Development Framework
frameworks.coverage: Complete publisher OSCAL index, including groups and nested controls/enhancements. Withdrawn entries are marked deprecated. Discovery summaries are not complete control text.

frameworks.name: OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10
frameworks.coverage: All 10 categories in the 2026 edition. Catalog v1 retains the different 2025 numbering.

frameworks.name: OWASP Top 10
frameworks.coverage: All 10 categories and publisher-listed CWE cross-references.

frameworks.name: PCI Data Security Standard
frameworks.coverage: All 12 top-level requirement areas with editorial labels. Detailed subrequirements, testing procedures and licensed text are not bundled.

frameworks.name: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (SOC 2)
frameworks.coverage: All five public trust-service categories. Detailed licensed criteria and points of focus are not bundled.

entries.name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
entries.description: The product uses a cookie to store sensitive information, but the cookie is not marked with the HttpOnly flag.

entries.name: Insufficient Visual Distinction of Homoglyphs Presented to User
entries.description: The product displays information or identifiers to a user, but the display mechanism does not make it easy for the user to distinguish between visually similar or identical glyphs (homoglyphs), which may cause the user to misinterpret a glyph and perform an unintended, insecure action.

entries.name: Struts: Duplicate Validation Forms
entries.description: The product uses multiple Struts validation forms with the same name.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames
entries.description: The web application does not restrict or incorrectly restricts frame objects or UI layers that belong to another application or domain.

entries.name: Use of Web Link to Untrusted Target with window.opener Access
entries.description: The web application produces links to untrusted external sites outside of its sphere of control, but it does not properly prevent the external site from modifying security-critical properties of the window.opener object, such as the location property.

entries.name: Incomplete Comparison with Missing Factors
entries.description: The product performs a comparison between entities that must consider multiple factors or characteristics of each entity, but the comparison does not include one or more of these factors.

entries.name: Comparison of Incompatible Types
entries.description: The product performs a comparison between two entities, but the entities are of different, incompatible types that cannot be guaranteed to provide correct results when they are directly compared.

entries.name: Comparison Using Wrong Factors
entries.description: The code performs a comparison between two entities, but the comparison examines the wrong factors or characteristics of the entities.

entries.name: Struts: Incomplete validate() Method Definition
entries.description: The product has a validator form that either does not define a validate() method, or defines a validate() method but does not call super.validate().

entries.name: Processor Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code
entries.description: The developer builds a security-critical protection mechanism into the software, but the processor optimizes the execution of the program such that the mechanism is removed or modified.

entries.name: Insecure Automated Optimizations
entries.description: The product uses a mechanism that automatically optimizes code, e.g. to improve a characteristic such as performance, but the optimizations can have an unintended side effect that might violate an intended security assumption.

entries.name: Inadequate Detection or Handling of Adversarial Input Perturbations in Automated Recognition Mechanism
entries.description: The product uses an automated mechanism such as machine learning to recognize complex data inputs (e.g. image or audio) as a particular concept or category, but it does not properly detect or handle inputs that have been modified or constructed in a way that causes the mechanism to detect a different, incorrect concept.

entries.name: Struts: Form Bean Does Not Extend Validation Class
entries.description: If a form bean does not extend an ActionForm subclass of the Validator framework, it can expose the application to other weaknesses related to insufficient input validation.

entries.name: Use of Redundant Code
entries.description: The product has multiple functions, methods, procedures, macros, etc. that contain the same code, i.e., the code has been copied or duplicated.

entries.name: Static Member Data Element outside of a Singleton Class Element
entries.description: The code contains a member element that is declared as static (but not final), in which its parent class element is not a singleton class - that is, a class element that can be used only once in the 'to' association of a Create action.

entries.name: Data Element Aggregating an Excessively Large Number of Non-Primitive Elements
entries.description: The product uses a data element that has an excessively large number of sub-elements with non-primitive data types such as structures or aggregated objects.

entries.name: Architecture with Number of Horizontal Layers Outside of Expected Range
entries.description: The product's architecture contains too many - or too few - horizontal layers.

entries.name: Parent Class with a Virtual Destructor and a Child Class without a Virtual Destructor
entries.description: A parent class has a virtual destructor method, but the parent has a child class that does not have a virtual destructor.

entries.name: Creation of Immutable Text Using String Concatenation
entries.description: The product creates an immutable text string using string concatenation operations.

entries.name: Modules with Circular Dependencies
entries.description: The product contains modules in which one module has references that cycle back to itself, i.e., there are circular dependencies.

entries.name: Invokable Control Element with Large Number of Outward Calls
entries.description: The code contains callable control elements that contain an excessively large number of references to other application objects external to the context of the callable, i.e. a Fan-Out value that is excessively large.

entries.name: Excessive Data Query Operations in a Large Data Table
