entries.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
entries.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

entries.name: Missing Standardized Error Handling Mechanism
entries.description: The product does not use a standardized method for handling errors throughout the code.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Use of Dynamic Class Loading
entries.description: This weakness has been deprecated because it partially overlaps CWE-470, it describes legitimate programmer behavior, and other portions will need to be integrated into other entries.

entries.name: Suspicious Comment
entries.description: The code contains comments that suggest the presence of bugs, incomplete functionality, or weaknesses.

entries.name: Use of Hard-coded, Security-relevant Constants
entries.description: The product uses hard-coded constants instead of symbolic names for security-critical values, which increases the likelihood of mistakes during code maintenance or security policy change.

entries.name: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing
entries.description: The product inappropriately exposes a directory listing with an index of all the resources located inside of the directory.

entries.name: Missing Password Field Masking
entries.description: The product does not mask passwords during entry, increasing the potential for attackers to observe and capture passwords.

entries.name: Path Equivalence: '/./' (Single Dot Directory)
entries.description: The product accepts path input in the form of single dot directory exploit ('/./') without appropriate validation, which can lead to ambiguous path resolution and allow an attacker to traverse the file system to unintended locations or access arbitrary files.

entries.name: Server-generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
entries.description: Certain conditions, such as network failure, will cause a server error message to be displayed.

entries.name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Authorization Before Parsing and Canonicalization
entries.description: If a web server does not fully parse requested URLs before it examines them for authorization, it may be possible for an attacker to bypass authorization protection.

entries.name: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties
entries.description: The product makes files or directories accessible to unauthorized actors, even though they should not be.

entries.name: Command Shell in Externally Accessible Directory
entries.description: A possible shell file exists in /cgi-bin/ or other accessible directories. This is extremely dangerous and can be used by an attacker to execute commands on the web server.

entries.name: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Not Using Input Validation Framework
entries.description: The ASP.NET application does not use an input validation framework.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Plaintext Password in Configuration File
entries.description: The J2EE application stores a plaintext password in a configuration file.

entries.name: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Use of Identity Impersonation
entries.description: Configuring an ASP.NET application to run with impersonated credentials may give the application unnecessary privileges.

entries.name: Use of getlogin() in Multithreaded Application
entries.description: The product uses the getlogin() function in a multithreaded context, potentially causing it to return incorrect values.

entries.name: Path Equivalence: 'filedir*' (Wildcard)
entries.description: The product accepts path input in the form of asterisk wildcard ('filedir*') without appropriate validation, which can lead to ambiguous path resolution and allow an attacker to traverse the file system to unintended locations or access arbitrary files.

entries.name: Use of umask() with chmod-style Argument
entries.description: The product calls umask() with an incorrect argument that is specified as if it is an argument to chmod().

entries.name: Dead Code
entries.description: The product contains dead code, which can never be executed.

entries.name: Return of Stack Variable Address
entries.description: A function returns the address of a stack variable.

entries.name: Assignment to Variable without Use
entries.description: The variable's value is assigned but never used, i.e., is a dead store. That is, after the assignment, the variable is either assigned another value or goes out of scope.

entries.name: Use of Hibernate with HQL/SQL Query String Containing External Input
entries.description: The product uses Hibernate to execute a dynamic HQL or SQL statement, but the statement is built with user-controlled input.

entries.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking
entries.description: The product relies on the existence or values of cookies when performing security-critical operations, but it does not properly ensure that the setting is valid for the associated user.

entries.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled SQL Primary Key
entries.description: The product uses a database table that includes records that should not be accessible to an actor, but it executes a SQL statement with a primary key that can be controlled by that actor.

entries.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
entries.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

entries.name: finalize() Method Without super.finalize()
entries.description: The product contains a finalize() method that does not call super.finalize().

entries.name: Path Equivalence: 'fakedir/../realdir/filename'
entries.description: The product contains protection mechanisms to restrict access to 'realdir/filename', but it constructs pathnames using external input in the form of 'fakedir/../realdir/filename' that are not handled by those mechanisms. This allows attackers to perform unauthorized actions against the targeted file.

entries.name: Expression is Always False
entries.description: The product contains an expression that will always evaluate to false.

entries.name: Expression is Always True
entries.description: The product contains an expression that will always evaluate to true.

entries.name: Call to Thread run() instead of start()
entries.description: The product calls a thread's run() method instead of calling start().

entries.name: Improper Following of Specification by Caller
entries.description: The product does not follow or incorrectly follows the specifications as required by the implementation language, environment, framework, protocol, or platform.

entries.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Synchronization Primitives
entries.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using thread synchronization primitives.

entries.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of AWT Swing
entries.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using AWT/Swing.

entries.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Java I/O
entries.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using the java.io package.

entries.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Sockets
entries.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using sockets.

entries.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Class Loader
entries.description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using the class loader.

entries.name: J2EE Bad Practices: Non-serializable Object Stored in Session
entries.description: The product stores a non-serializable object as an HttpSession attribute.

entries.name: Path Equivalence: Windows 8.3 Filename
entries.description: The product contains a protection mechanism that restricts access to a long filename on a Windows operating system, but it does not properly restrict access to the equivalent short "8.3" filename.

entries.name: clone() Method Without super.clone()
entries.description: The product contains a clone() method that does not call super.clone() to obtain the new object.

entries.name: Object Model Violation: Just One of Equals and Hashcode Defined
entries.description: The product does not maintain equal hashcodes for equal objects.

entries.name: Array Declared Public, Final, and Static
entries.description: The product declares an array public, final, and static, which is not sufficient to prevent the array's contents from being modified.

entries.name: finalize() Method Declared Public
entries.description: The product violates secure coding principles for mobile code by declaring a finalize() method public.

entries.name: Return Inside Finally Block
entries.description: The code has a return statement inside a finally block.

entries.name: Empty Synchronized Block
entries.description: The product contains an empty synchronized block.

entries.name: Explicit Call to Finalize()
entries.description: The product makes an explicit call to the finalize() method from outside the finalizer.

entries.name: Assignment of a Fixed Address to a Pointer
entries.description: The product sets a pointer to a specific address other than NULL or 0.

entries.name: Attempt to Access Child of a Non-structure Pointer
entries.description: The product casts a non-structure type to a structure type, then accesses a field within the structure.

entries.name: Call to Non-ubiquitous API
entries.description: The product uses an API function that does not exist on all versions of the target platform.

entries.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access
entries.description: The product attempts to access a file based on the filename, but it does not properly prevent that filename from identifying a link or shortcut that resolves to an unintended resource.

entries.name: Free of Memory not on the Heap
entries.description: The product calls free() on a pointer to memory that was not allocated using associated heap allocation functions such as malloc(), calloc(), or realloc().

entries.name: Sensitive Data Storage in Improperly Locked Memory
entries.description: The product stores sensitive data in memory that is not locked, or that has been incorrectly locked.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Authentication Bypass Issues
entries.description: This weakness has been deprecated because it covered redundant concepts already described in CWE-287.

entries.name: Authentication Bypass: OpenSSL CTX Object Modified after SSL Objects are Created
entries.description: The product modifies the SSL context after connection creation has begun.

entries.name: J2EE Framework: Saving Unserializable Objects to Disk
entries.description: The J2EE container attempts to write unserializable objects to disk.

entries.name: Comparison of Object References Instead of Object Contents
entries.description: The product compares object references instead of the contents of the objects themselves, preventing it from detecting equivalent objects.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Incorrect Semantic Object Comparison
entries.description: This weakness has been deprecated. It was poorly described and difficult to distinguish from other entries. It was also inappropriate to assign a separate ID solely because of domain-specific considerations. Its closest equivalent is CWE-1023.

entries.name: Use of Wrong Operator in String Comparison
entries.description: The product uses the wrong operator when comparing a string, such as using "==" when the .equals() method should be used instead.

entries.name: Use of HTTP Request With Sensitive Query String
entries.description: The web application uses an HTTP method to process a request, but the request includes sensitive information in the query string.

entries.name: Missing Validation of OpenSSL Certificate
entries.description: The product uses OpenSSL and trusts or uses a certificate without using the SSL_get_verify_result() function to ensure that the certificate satisfies all necessary security requirements.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Insufficient Session-ID Length
entries.description: The J2EE application is configured to use an insufficient session ID length.

entries.name: Uncaught Exception in Servlet
entries.description: The Servlet does not catch all exceptions.

entries.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site
entries.description: The web application accepts a user-controlled input that specifies a link to an external site, and uses that link in a redirect.

entries.name: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security
entries.description: The product includes a server that relies on the client to implement a protection mechanism that is intended to protect the server.

entries.name: Use of Client-Side Authentication
entries.description: A client/server product performs authentication within client code but not in server code, allowing server-side authentication to be bypassed via a modified client that omits the authentication check.

entries.name: Multiple Binds to the Same Port
entries.description: When multiple sockets are allowed to bind to the same port, other services on that port may be stolen or spoofed.

entries.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
entries.description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

entries.name: Public Static Final Field References Mutable Object
entries.description: A public or protected static final field references a mutable object, which allows the object to be changed by malicious code, or accidentally from another package.

entries.name: Struts: Non-private Field in ActionForm Class
entries.description: The product uses an ActionForm class that contains a field that has not been declared private.

entries.name: Double-Checked Locking
entries.description: The product uses double-checked locking to access a resource without the overhead of explicit synchronization, but the locking is insufficient.

entries.name: UNIX Symbolic Link (Symlink) Following
entries.description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently account for when the file is a symbolic link that resolves to a target outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

entries.name: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere
entries.description: The product uses an externally controlled name or reference that resolves to a resource that is outside of the intended control sphere.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
entries.description: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.

entries.name: Improper Authorization of Index Containing Sensitive Information
entries.description: The product creates a search index of private or sensitive documents, but it does not properly limit index access to actors who are authorized to see the original information.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Insufficient Session Expiration
entries.description: This entry has been deprecated because it was insufficiently clear. Consider CWE-1462 and its descendants.

entries.name: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
entries.description: The Secure attribute for sensitive cookies in HTTPS sessions is not set.

entries.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code Comments
entries.description: The product's source code includes comments that contain sensitive information, such as filenames related to the application, old links or links that were not meant to be browsed by users, old code fragments, etc.

entries.name: Incomplete Identification of Uploaded File Variables (PHP)
entries.description: The PHP application uses an old method for processing uploaded files by referencing the four global variables that are set for each file (e.g. $varname, $varname_size, $varname_name, $varname_type).

entries.name: Reachable Assertion
entries.description: The product contains an assert() or similar statement that can be triggered by an attacker, which leads to an application exit or other behavior that is more severe than necessary.

entries.name: Exposed Unsafe ActiveX Method
entries.description: An ActiveX control is intended for use in a web browser, but it exposes dangerous methods that perform actions that are outside of the browser's security model (e.g. the zone or domain).

entries.name: Dangling Database Cursor
entries.description: The product does not close a database cursor properly, leaving the cursor "dangling."

entries.name: UNIX Hard Link
entries.description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently account for when the name is associated with a hard link to a target that is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

entries.name: Unverified Password Change
entries.description: When setting a new password for a user, the product does not require knowledge of the original password, or using another form of authentication.

entries.name: Variable Extraction Error
entries.description: The product uses external input to determine the names of variables into which information is extracted, without verifying that the names of the specified variables are valid.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Function Hook Arguments
entries.description: The product adds hooks to user-accessible API functions, but it does not properly validate the arguments.

entries.name: Unsafe ActiveX Control Marked Safe For Scripting
entries.description: The product includes an ActiveX control that is intended for restricted use, but the control has been marked as safe-for-scripting.

entries.name: Executable Regular Expression Error
entries.description: The product uses a regular expression that either (1) contains an executable component with user-controlled inputs, or (2) allows a user to enable execution by inserting pattern modifiers.

entries.name: Permissive Regular Expression
entries.description: The product uses a regular expression that does not sufficiently restrict the set of allowed values.

entries.name: Null Byte Interaction Error (Poison Null Byte)
entries.description: The product does not properly handle null bytes or NUL characters when passing data between different representations or components.

entries.name: Dynamic Variable Evaluation
entries.description: In a language where the user can influence the name of a variable at runtime, if the variable names are not controlled, an attacker can read or write to arbitrary variables, or access arbitrary functions.

entries.name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
entries.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine with arguments that are not correctly specified.

entries.name: Not Failing Securely
entries.description: When the product encounters an error condition or failure, its design requires it to fall back to a state that is less secure than other options that are available, such as selecting the weakest encryption algorithm or using the most permissive access control restrictions.

entries.name: Unnecessary Complexity in Protection Mechanism (Not Using 'Economy of Mechanism')
entries.description: The product uses a more complex mechanism than necessary, which could lead to resultant weaknesses when the mechanism is not correctly understood, modeled, configured, implemented, or used.

entries.name: Not Using Complete Mediation
entries.description: The product does not perform access checks on a resource every time the resource is accessed by an entity, which can create resultant weaknesses if that entity's rights or privileges change over time.

entries.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
entries.description: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

entries.name: Windows Shortcut Following (.LNK)
entries.description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently handle when the file is a Windows shortcut (.LNK) whose target is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

entries.name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
entries.description: The product contains a mechanism for users to recover or change their passwords without knowing the original password, but the mechanism is weak.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Names for Files and Other Resources
entries.description: The product constructs the name of a file or other resource using input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the resulting name.

entries.name: External Control of Critical State Data
entries.description: The product stores security-critical state information about its users, or the product itself, in a location that is accessible to unauthorized actors.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions
entries.description: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XPath expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax
entries.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes web scripting syntax in HTTP headers that can be used by web browser components that can process raw headers, such as Flash.

entries.name: Overly Restrictive Account Lockout Mechanism
entries.description: The product contains an account lockout protection mechanism, but the mechanism is too restrictive and can be triggered too easily, which allows attackers to deny service to legitimate users by causing their accounts to be locked out.

entries.name: Reliance on File Name or Extension of Externally-Supplied File
entries.description: The product allows a file to be uploaded, but it relies on the file name or extension of the file to determine the appropriate behaviors.

entries.name: Use of Non-Canonical URL Paths for Authorization Decisions
entries.description: The product defines policy namespaces and makes authorization decisions based on the assumption that a URL is canonical.

entries.name: Incorrect Use of Privileged APIs
entries.description: The product does not conform to the API requirements for a function call that requires extra privileges. This could allow attackers to gain privileges by causing the function to be called incorrectly.

entries.name: Reliance on Obfuscation or Encryption of Security-Relevant Inputs without Integrity Checking
entries.description: The product uses obfuscation or encryption of inputs that should not be mutable by an external actor, but the product does not use integrity checks to detect if those inputs have been modified.

entries.name: Windows Hard Link
entries.description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently handle when the name is associated with a hard link to a target that is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

entries.name: Trusting HTTP Permission Methods on the Server Side
entries.description: The server contains a protection mechanism that assumes that any URI that is accessed using HTTP GET will not cause a state change to the associated resource.

entries.name: Exposure of WSDL File Containing Sensitive Information
entries.description: The Web services architecture may require exposing a Web Service Definition Language (WSDL) file that contains information on the publicly accessible services and how callers of these services should interact with them (e.g. what parameters they expect and what types they return).

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions
entries.description: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XQuery expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input.

entries.name: Improper Isolation or Compartmentalization
entries.description: The product does not properly compartmentalize or isolate functionality, processes, or resources that require different privilege levels, rights, or permissions.

entries.name: Reliance on a Single Factor in a Security Decision
entries.description: A protection mechanism relies exclusively, or to a large extent, on the evaluation of a single condition or the integrity of a single object or entity in order to make a decision about granting access to restricted resources or functionality.

entries.name: Insufficient Psychological Acceptability
entries.description: The product has a protection mechanism that is too difficult or inconvenient to use, encouraging non-malicious users to disable or bypass the mechanism, whether by accident or on purpose.

entries.name: Reliance on Security Through Obscurity
entries.description: The product uses a protection mechanism whose strength depends heavily on its obscurity, such that knowledge of its algorithms or key data is sufficient to defeat the mechanism.

entries.name: Violation of Secure Design Principles
entries.description: The product violates well-established principles for secure design.

entries.name: Improper Handling of File Names that Identify Virtual Resources
entries.description: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles a file name that identifies a "virtual" resource that is not directly specified within the directory that is associated with the file name.

entries.name: Improper Synchronization
entries.description: The product utilizes multiple threads, processes, components, or systems to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

entries.name: Use of a Non-reentrant Function in a Concurrent Context
entries.description: The product calls a non-reentrant function in a concurrent context in which a competing code sequence (e.g. thread or signal handler) may have an opportunity to call the same function or otherwise influence its state.

entries.name: Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime
entries.description: The product does not maintain or incorrectly maintains control over a resource throughout its lifetime of creation, use, and release.

entries.name: Improper Initialization
entries.description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource.

entries.name: Operation on Resource in Wrong Phase of Lifetime
entries.description: The product performs an operation on a resource at the wrong phase of the resource's lifecycle, which can lead to unexpected behaviors.

entries.name: Improper Locking
entries.description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

entries.name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
entries.description: The product exposes a resource to the wrong control sphere, providing unintended actors with inappropriate access to the resource.

entries.name: Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres
entries.description: The product does not properly transfer a resource/behavior to another sphere, or improperly imports a resource/behavior from another sphere, in a manner that provides unintended control over that resource.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Windows Device Names
entries.description: The product constructs pathnames from user input, but it does not handle or incorrectly handles a pathname containing a Windows device name such as AUX or CON. This typically leads to denial of service or an information exposure when the application attempts to process the pathname as a regular file.

entries.name: Always-Incorrect Control Flow Implementation
entries.description: The code contains a control flow path that does not reflect the algorithm that the path is intended to implement, leading to incorrect behavior any time this path is navigated.

entries.name: Lack of Administrator Control over Security
entries.description: The product uses security features in a way that prevents the product's administrator from tailoring security settings to reflect the environment in which the product is being used.

entries.name: Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release
entries.description: The product uses, accesses, or otherwise operates on a resource after that resource has been expired, released, or revoked.

entries.name: External Influence of Sphere Definition
entries.description: The product does not prevent the definition of control spheres from external actors.

entries.name: Uncontrolled Recursion
entries.description: The product does not properly control the amount of recursion that takes place, consuming excessive resources, such as allocated memory or the program stack.

entries.name: Multiple Operations on Resource in Single-Operation Context
entries.description: The product performs the same operation on a resource two or more times, when the operation should only be applied once.

entries.name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
entries.description: The product invokes a potentially dangerous function that could introduce a vulnerability if it is used incorrectly, but the function can also be used safely.

entries.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Overflow
entries.description: The product performs a calculation to determine how much memory to allocate, but an integer overflow can occur that causes less memory to be allocated than expected, leading to a buffer overflow.

entries.name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
entries.description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.

entries.name: Incorrect Calculation
entries.description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrect Order of Arguments
entries.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies the arguments in an incorrect order.

entries.name: Incorrect Provision of Specified Functionality
entries.description: The code does not function according to its published specifications, potentially leading to incorrect usage.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
entries.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies too many arguments, or too few arguments, which may lead to undefined behavior and resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrect Argument Type
entries.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies an argument that is the wrong data type, which may lead to resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrectly Specified Argument Value
entries.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies an argument that contains the wrong value, which may lead to resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrect Variable or Reference as Argument
entries.description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies the wrong variable or reference as one of the arguments, which may lead to undefined behavior and resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Permission Race Condition During Resource Copy
entries.description: The product, while copying or cloning a resource, does not set the resource's permissions or access control until the copy is complete, leaving the resource exposed to other spheres while the copy is taking place.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Windows ::DATA Alternate Data Stream
entries.description: The product does not properly prevent access to, or detect usage of, alternate data streams (ADS).

entries.name: Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference
entries.description: The product does not check for an error after calling a function that can return with a NULL pointer if the function fails, which leads to a resultant NULL pointer dereference.

entries.name: Insufficient Control Flow Management
entries.description: The code does not sufficiently manage its control flow during execution, creating conditions in which the control flow can be modified in unexpected ways.

entries.name: Incomplete Denylist to Cross-Site Scripting
entries.description: The product uses a denylist-based protection mechanism to defend against XSS attacks, but the denylist is incomplete.

entries.name: Protection Mechanism Failure
entries.description: The product does not use or incorrectly uses a protection mechanism that provides sufficient defense against directed attacks against the product.

entries.name: Use of Multiple Resources with Duplicate Identifier
entries.description: The product uses multiple resources that can have the same identifier, in a context in which unique identifiers are required.

entries.name: Use of Low-Level Functionality
entries.description: The product uses low-level functionality that is explicitly prohibited by the framework or specification under which the product is supposed to operate.

entries.name: Incorrect Behavior Order
entries.description: The product performs multiple related behaviors, but the behaviors are performed in the wrong order in ways that may produce resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Incorrect Comparison
entries.description: The product compares two entities in a security-relevant context, but the comparison is incorrect.

entries.name: Execution After Redirect (EAR)
entries.description: The web application sends a redirect to another location, but instead of exiting, it executes additional code.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Missing Custom Error Page
entries.description: The product has a J2EE component that does not have a custom error page.

entries.name: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
entries.description: The product does not properly anticipate or handle exceptional conditions that rarely occur during normal operation of the product.

entries.name: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
entries.description: The product does not correctly convert an object, resource, or structure from one type to a different type.

entries.name: Incorrect Control Flow Scoping
entries.description: The product does not properly return control flow to the proper location after it has completed a task or detected an unusual condition.

entries.name: Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference
entries.description: The product uses a name or reference to access a resource, but the name/reference resolves to a resource that is outside of the intended control sphere.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization
entries.description: The product does not ensure or incorrectly ensures that structured messages or data are well-formed and that certain security properties are met before being used when received from an upstream component, or before being sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Incorrect Ownership Assignment
entries.description: The product assigns an owner to a resource, but the owner is outside of the intended control sphere.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Apple '.DS_Store'
entries.description: This entry has been deprecated as it represents a specific observed example of a UNIX Hard Link weakness type rather than its own individual weakness type. Please refer to CWE-62.

entries.name: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
entries.description: The product does not follow certain coding rules for development.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Apple HFS+ Alternate Data Stream Path
entries.description: The product does not properly handle special paths that may identify the data or resource fork of a file on the HFS+ file system.

entries.name: External Control of File Name or Path
entries.description: The product allows user input to control or influence paths or file names that are used in filesystem operations.

entries.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
entries.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

entries.name: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code
entries.description: The developer builds a security-critical protection mechanism into the software, but the compiler optimizes the program such that the mechanism is removed or modified.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component
entries.description: The product constructs all or part of a command, data structure, or record using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify how it is parsed or interpreted when it is sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
entries.description: The product provides an Applications Programming Interface (API) or similar interface for interaction with external actors, but the interface includes a dangerous method or function that is not properly restricted.

entries.name: Failure to Sanitize Special Elements into a Different Plane
entries.description: The product does not adequately filter user-controlled input for special elements with control implications.

entries.name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
entries.description: The product does not check or incorrectly checks for unusual or exceptional conditions that are not expected to occur frequently during day to day operation of the product.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
entries.description: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles an exceptional condition.

entries.name: Missing Custom Error Page
entries.description: The product does not return custom error pages to the user, possibly exposing sensitive information.

entries.name: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation
entries.description: A protocol or its implementation supports interaction between multiple actors and allows those actors to negotiate which algorithm should be used in a protection mechanism such as encryption or authentication, but it does not select the strongest algorithm that is available to both parties.

entries.name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
entries.description: The product uses an API function, data structure, or other entity in a way that relies on properties that are not always guaranteed to hold for that entity.

entries.name: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt
entries.description: The product uses a one-way cryptographic hash against an input that should not be reversible, such as a password, but the product does not also use a salt as part of the input.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Equivalent Special Elements
entries.description: The product correctly neutralizes certain special elements, but it improperly neutralizes equivalent special elements.

entries.name: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt
entries.description: The product uses a one-way cryptographic hash against an input that should not be reversible, such as a password, but the product uses a predictable salt as part of the input.

entries.name: Free of Pointer not at Start of Buffer
entries.description: The product calls free() on a pointer to a memory resource that was allocated on the heap, but the pointer is not at the start of the buffer.

entries.name: Mismatched Memory Management Routines
entries.description: The product attempts to return a memory resource to the system, but it calls a release function that is not compatible with the function that was originally used to allocate that resource.

entries.name: Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference
entries.description: The product attempts to return a memory resource to the system, but it calls the wrong release function or calls the appropriate release function incorrectly.

entries.name: Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource
entries.description: The product locks a critical resource more times than intended, leading to an unexpected state in the system.

entries.name: Multiple Unlocks of a Critical Resource
entries.description: The product unlocks a critical resource more times than intended, leading to an unexpected state in the system.

entries.name: Critical Data Element Declared Public
entries.description: The product declares a critical variable, field, or member to be public when intended security policy requires it to be private.

entries.name: Access to Critical Private Variable via Public Method
entries.description: The product defines a public method that reads or modifies a private variable.

entries.name: Incorrect Short Circuit Evaluation
entries.description: The product contains a conditional statement with multiple logical expressions in which one of the non-leading expressions may produce side effects.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Uncontrolled File Descriptor Consumption
entries.description: This entry has been deprecated because it was a duplicate of CWE-774. All content has been transferred to CWE-774.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command
entries.description: The product constructs all or part of a command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended command when it is sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
entries.description: The product allocates a reusable resource or group of resources on behalf of an actor without imposing any intended restrictions on the size or number of resources that can be allocated.

entries.name: Missing Reference to Active Allocated Resource
entries.description: The product does not properly maintain a reference to a resource that has been allocated, which prevents the resource from being reclaimed.

entries.name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
entries.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

entries.name: Missing Reference to Active File Descriptor or Handle
entries.description: The product does not properly maintain references to a file descriptor or handle, which prevents that file descriptor/handle from being reclaimed.

entries.name: Allocation of File Descriptors or Handles Without Limits or Throttling
entries.description: The product allocates file descriptors or handles on behalf of an actor without imposing any restrictions on how many descriptors can be allocated, in violation of the intended security policy for that actor.

entries.name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
entries.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs
entries.description: The product uses XML documents and allows their structure to be defined with a Document Type Definition (DTD), but it does not properly control the number of recursive definitions of entities.

entries.name: Regular Expression without Anchors
entries.description: The product uses a regular expression to perform neutralization, but the regular expression omits one or more anchors that may allow malicious or malformed data to slip through.

entries.name: Insufficient Logging
entries.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

entries.name: Logging of Excessive Data
entries.description: The product logs too much information, making log files hard to process and possibly hindering recovery efforts or forensic analysis after an attack.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
entries.description: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command before it is sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP
entries.description: The product uses the RSA algorithm but does not incorporate Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding (OAEP).

entries.name: Improper Address Validation in IOCTL with METHOD_NEITHER I/O Control Code
entries.description: The product defines an IOCTL that uses METHOD_NEITHER for I/O, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates the addresses that are provided.

entries.name: Exposed IOCTL with Insufficient Access Control
entries.description: The product implements an IOCTL with functionality that should be restricted, but it does not properly enforce access control for the IOCTL.

entries.name: Operator Precedence Logic Error
entries.description: The product uses an expression in which operator precedence causes incorrect logic to be used.

entries.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking in a Security Decision
entries.description: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of a cookie, but it does not properly ensure that the cookie is valid for the associated user.

entries.name: Use of Path Manipulation Function without Maximum-sized Buffer
entries.description: The product invokes a function for normalizing paths or file names, but it provides an output buffer that is smaller than the maximum possible size, such as PATH_MAX.

entries.name: Access of Memory Location Before Start of Buffer
entries.description: The product reads or writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location prior to the beginning of the buffer.

entries.name: Out-of-bounds Write
entries.description: The product writes data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.

entries.name: Access of Memory Location After End of Buffer
entries.description: The product reads or writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location after the end of the buffer.

entries.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
entries.description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
entries.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

entries.name: Improper Filtering of Special Elements
entries.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but it does not filter or incorrectly filters special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Incomplete Filtering of Special Elements
entries.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but it does not completely filter special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Incomplete Filtering of One or More Instances of Special Elements
entries.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not completely filter one or more instances of special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Only Filtering One Instance of a Special Element
entries.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only filters a single instance of a special element before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Incomplete Filtering of Multiple Instances of Special Elements
entries.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but it does not filter all instances of a special element before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Only Filtering Special Elements at a Specified Location
entries.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements at a specified location, thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Only Filtering Special Elements Relative to a Marker
entries.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements positioned relative to a marker (e.g. "at the beginning/end of a string; the second argument"), thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Only Filtering Special Elements at an Absolute Position
entries.description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements at an absolute position (e.g. "byte number 10"), thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
entries.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

entries.name: Improper Control of Interaction Frequency
entries.description: The product does not properly limit the number or frequency of interactions that it has with an actor, such as the number of incoming requests.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Entity Bean Declared Remote
entries.description: The J2EE application exposes a remote interface for an entity bean, but it also exposes methods that get or set the bean's data.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page
entries.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special characters such as "", and "&" that could be interpreted as web-scripting elements when they are sent to a downstream component that processes web pages.

entries.name: Guessable CAPTCHA
entries.description: The product uses a CAPTCHA challenge, but the challenge can be guessed or automatically recognized by a non-human actor.

entries.name: Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value
entries.description: The product uses a sequential operation to read or write a buffer, but it uses an incorrect length value that causes it to access memory that is outside of the bounds of the buffer.

entries.name: Buffer Access Using Size of Source Buffer
entries.description: The product uses the size of a source buffer when reading from or writing to a destination buffer, which may cause it to access memory that is outside of the bounds of the buffer.

entries.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
entries.description: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of an input, but the input can be modified by an untrusted actor in a way that bypasses the protection mechanism.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in an Error Message Web Page
entries.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special characters that could be interpreted as web-scripting elements when they are sent to an error page.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes of IMG Tags in a Web Page
entries.description: The web application does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes scripting elements within attributes of HTML IMG tags, such as the src attribute.

entries.name: Missing Synchronization
entries.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

entries.name: Incorrect Synchronization
entries.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.

entries.name: Untrusted Pointer Dereference
entries.description: The product obtains a value from an untrusted source, converts this value to a pointer, and dereferences the resulting pointer.

entries.name: Use of Out-of-range Pointer Offset
entries.description: The product performs pointer arithmetic on a valid pointer, but it uses an offset that can point outside of the intended range of valid memory locations for the resulting pointer.

entries.name: Access of Uninitialized Pointer
entries.description: The product accesses or uses a pointer that has not been initialized.

entries.name: Expired Pointer Dereference
entries.description: The product dereferences a pointer that contains a location for memory that was previously valid, but is no longer valid.

entries.name: Premature Release of Resource During Expected Lifetime
entries.description: The product releases a resource that is still intended to be used by itself or another actor.

entries.name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
entries.description: The product does not restrict a reference to a Document Type Definition (DTD) to the intended control sphere. This might allow attackers to reference arbitrary DTDs, possibly causing the product to expose files, consume excessive system resources, or execute arbitrary http requests on behalf of the attacker.

entries.name: Signal Handler with Functionality that is not Asynchronous-Safe
entries.description: The product defines a signal handler that contains code sequences that are not asynchronous-safe, i.e., the functionality is not reentrant, or it can be interrupted.

entries.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
entries.description: The product imports, requires, or includes executable functionality (such as a library) from a source that is outside of the intended control sphere.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes in a Web Page
entries.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes "javascript:" or other URIs from dangerous attributes within tags, such as onmouseover, onload, onerror, or style.

entries.name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
entries.description: The product includes web functionality (such as a web widget) from another domain in a way that causes the functionality to operate within the domain of the product, potentially granting total access and control of the product to the untrusted source.

entries.name: Signal Handler Function Associated with Multiple Signals
entries.description: The product defines a function that is used as a handler for more than one signal.

entries.name: Unlock of a Resource that is not Locked
entries.description: The product attempts to unlock a resource that is not locked.

entries.name: Deadlock
entries.description: The product contains multiple threads or executable segments that are waiting for each other to release a necessary lock, resulting in deadlock.

entries.name: Excessive Iteration
entries.description: The product performs an iteration or loop without sufficiently limiting the number of times that the loop is executed.

entries.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition
entries.description: The product contains an iteration or loop with an exit condition that cannot be reached, i.e., an infinite loop.

entries.name: Use of Password Hash Instead of Password for Authentication
entries.description: The product includes a client that computes a hash of a password and sends the hash to another component, which compares the supplied hash to the hash obtained from a data store of password hashes.

entries.name: Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action
entries.description: The product requires that an actor should only be able to perform an action once, or to have only one unique action, but the product does not enforce or incorrectly enforces this restriction.

entries.name: Inappropriate Encoding for Output Context
entries.description: The product uses or specifies an encoding when generating output to a downstream component, but the specified encoding is not the same as the encoding that is expected by the downstream component.

entries.name: Numeric Range Comparison Without Minimum Check
entries.description: The product checks a value to ensure that it is less than or equal to a maximum, but it does not also verify that the value is greater than or equal to the minimum.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Encoded URI Schemes in a Web Page
entries.description: The web application improperly neutralizes user-controlled input for executable script disguised with URI encodings.

entries.name: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow
entries.description: The product supports a session in which more than one behavior must be performed by an actor, but it does not properly ensure that the actor performs the behaviors in the required sequence or timeframe.

entries.name: Placement of User into Incorrect Group
entries.description: The product or the administrator places a user into an incorrect group.

entries.name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type
entries.description: The product allocates or initializes a resource such as a pointer, object, or variable using one type, but it later accesses that resource using a type that is incompatible with the original type.

entries.name: Doubled Character XSS Manipulations
entries.description: The web application does not filter user-controlled input for executable script disguised using doubling of the involved characters.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Invalid Characters in Identifiers in Web Pages
entries.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes invalid characters or byte sequences in the middle of tag names, URI schemes, and other identifiers.

entries.name: Missing Authorization
entries.description: The product does not perform an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action.

entries.name: Incorrect Authorization
entries.description: The product performs an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action, but it does not correctly perform the check.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Alternate XSS Syntax
entries.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controlled input for alternate script syntax.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command
entries.description: The product constructs a string for a command to be executed by a separate component in another control sphere, but it does not properly delimit the intended arguments, options, or switches within that command string.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
entries.description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component. Without sufficient removal or quoting of SQL syntax in user-controllable inputs, the generated SQL query can cause those inputs to be interpreted as SQL instead of ordinary user data.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Weak Access Permissions for EJB Methods
entries.description: If elevated access rights are assigned to EJB methods, then an attacker can take advantage of the permissions to exploit the product.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query
entries.description: The product constructs all or part of an LDAP query using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended LDAP query when it is sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource
entries.description: The product uses or accesses a resource that has not been initialized.

entries.name: Missing Initialization of Resource
entries.description: The product does not initialize a critical resource.

entries.name: XML Injection
entries.description: The product does not properly neutralize special elements that are used in XML, allowing attackers to modify the syntax, content, or commands of the XML before it is processed by an end system.

entries.name: Use of Expired File Descriptor
entries.description: The product uses or accesses a file descriptor after it has been closed.

entries.name: Improper Update of Reference Count
entries.description: The product uses a reference count to manage a resource, but it does not update or incorrectly updates the reference count.

entries.name: Hidden Functionality
entries.description: The product contains functionality that is not documented, not part of the specification, and not accessible through an interface or command sequence that is obvious to the product's users or administrators.

entries.name: Improper Control of Dynamically-Managed Code Resources
entries.description: The product does not properly restrict reading from or writing to dynamically-managed code resources such as variables, objects, classes, attributes, functions, or executable instructions or statements.

entries.name: Improper Control of Dynamically-Identified Variables
entries.description: The product does not properly restrict reading from or writing to dynamically-identified variables.

entries.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
entries.description: The product receives input from an upstream component that specifies multiple attributes, properties, or fields that are to be initialized or updated in an object, but it does not properly control which attributes can be modified.

entries.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
entries.description: The product generates a hash for a password, but it uses a scheme that does not provide a sufficient level of computational effort that would make password cracking attacks infeasible or expensive.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement
entries.description: The product constructs all or part of an expression language (EL) statement in a framework such as a Java Server Page (JSP) using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended EL statement before it is executed.

entries.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
entries.description: The web server receives a URL or similar request from an upstream component and retrieves the contents of this URL, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the request is being sent to the expected destination.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Improper Sanitization of Custom Special Characters
entries.description: This entry has been deprecated. It originally came from PLOVER, which sometimes defined "other" and "miscellaneous" categories in order to satisfy exhaustiveness requirements for taxonomies. Within the context of CWE, the use of a more abstract entry is preferred in mapping situations. CWE-75 is a more appropriate mapping.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Power Consumption
entries.description: The product operates in an environment in which power is a limited resource that cannot be automatically replenished - or has financial restrictions - but the product does not properly restrict the amount of power that its operation consumes.

entries.name: Storage of Sensitive Data in a Mechanism without Access Control
entries.description: The product stores sensitive information in a file system or device that does not have built-in access control.

entries.name: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
entries.description: The product stores sensitive information without properly limiting read or write access by unauthorized actors.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
entries.description: The product establishes a communication channel to (or from) an endpoint for privileged or protected operations, but it does not properly ensure that it is communicating with the correct endpoint.

entries.name: Improper Enforcement of Message Integrity During Transmission in a Communication Channel
entries.description: The product establishes a communication channel with an endpoint and receives a message from that endpoint, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the message was not modified during transmission.

entries.name: Improper Verification of Intent by Broadcast Receiver
entries.description: The Android application uses a Broadcast Receiver that receives an Intent but does not properly verify that the Intent came from an authorized source.

entries.name: Improper Export of Android Application Components
entries.description: The Android application exports a component for use by other applications, but does not properly restrict which applications can launch the component or access the data it contains.

entries.name: Use of Implicit Intent for Sensitive Communication
entries.description: The Android application uses an implicit intent for transmitting sensitive data to other applications.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences
entries.description: The product uses CRLF (carriage return line feeds) as a special element, e.g. to separate lines or records, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes CRLF sequences from inputs.

entries.name: Improper Authorization in Handler for Custom URL Scheme
entries.description: The product uses a handler for a custom URL scheme, but it does not properly restrict which actors can invoke the handler using the scheme.

entries.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code
entries.description: The product constructs all or part of a code segment using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the syntax or behavior of the intended code segment.

entries.name: Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel
entries.description: The product establishes a communication channel to handle an incoming request that has been initiated by an actor, but it does not properly verify that the request is coming from the expected origin.

entries.name: Incorrectly Specified Destination in a Communication Channel
entries.description: The product creates a communication channel to initiate an outgoing request to an actor, but it does not correctly specify the intended destination for that actor.

entries.name: Permissive Cross-domain Security Policy with Untrusted Domains
entries.description: The product uses a web-client protection mechanism such as a Content Security Policy (CSP) or cross-domain policy file, but the policy includes untrusted domains with which the web client is allowed to communicate.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
entries.description: The product generates a query intended to access or manipulate data in a data store such as a database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that can modify the intended logic of the query.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code
entries.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes code syntax before using the input in a dynamic evaluation call (e.g. "eval").

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Statically Saved Code
entries.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes code syntax before inserting the input into an executable resource, such as a library, configuration file, or template.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Server-Side Includes (SSI) Within a Web Page
entries.description: The product generates a web page, but does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input that could be interpreted as a server-side include (SSI) directive.

entries.name: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program
entries.description: The PHP application receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before its usage in "require," "include," or similar functions.

entries.name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers
entries.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended control sphere.

entries.name: Limit Public Release of Information
entries.description: Limit the public release of technical information about the AI stack used in an organization's products or services. Technical knowledge of how AI is used can be leveraged by adversaries to perform targeting and tailor attacks to the target system. Additionally, consider limiting the release of organizational information - including physical locations, researcher names, and department structures - from which technical details such as AI techniques, model architectures, or datasets may be inferred.

entries.name: Limit Model Artifact Release
entries.description: Limit public release of technical project details including data, algorithms, model architectures, and model checkpoints that are used in production, or that are representative of those used in production.

entries.name: Predictive AI Output Obfuscation
entries.description: Reduce the fidelity and amount of information returned by predictive AI inference endpoints to make model discovery, extraction, replication, and black-box adversarial-example optimization more difficult. Limit outputs to those required by the application. Depending on the use case, this may include withholding or reducing the precision of confidence scores, logits, class rankings, labels, embeddings, or additional model metadata.

entries.name: Predictive AI Model Hardening
entries.description: Design and train predictive AI models to maintain intended performance when presented with adversarial examples. Adversarial examples may include digitally perturbed inputs or physical countermeasures intended to cause misclassification, missed detection, or another attacker-selected prediction. Robustness techniques may include adversarial training, robust model architectures, defensive distillation, and certified robustness methods.

entries.name: Limit AI Service Query Volume and Rate
entries.description: Limit the number and rate of requests that users can submit to an AI service. Apply limits by user, API key, tenant, device, or other authenticated identity. Use short-term rate, burst, and concurrency limits together with longer-term usage quotas. Query limits can increase the time and cost required to extract model information, optimize adversarial inputs, discover system behavior, verify attacks, or overwhelm a service. Monitor for attempts to evade limits through distributed requests, account rotation, or stolen credentials. Query limits may not protect against attacks that require few req

entries.name: Control Access to AI Models and Data at Rest
entries.description: Establish access controls on internal model registries and limit internal access to production models. Limit access to training data only to approved users.

entries.name: Predictive AI Ensembles
entries.description: Use an ensemble of diverse predictive AI models to reduce reliance on a single model or model family and improve robustness against adversarial examples. Ensemble members should be sufficiently diverse, such as through different architectures, training procedures, features, or model families. Combine their predictions using an aggregation or adjudication method designed to prevent an adversarial example that evades one model from controlling the system's predictions.

entries.name: Sanitize Training Data
entries.description: Detect, quarantine, and remove or remediate poisoned data before it is used to train an AI model. Apply screening when datasets are acquired or updated, and before new data is incorporated into active learning workflows. Inspect data samples, annotations, and metadata for evidence of manipulation. Depending on the data and intended task, checks may include label inconsistencies, anomalous samples, unexpected shifts in source or class distributions, suspicious duplication or repeated patterns, and backdoor triggers. Compare findings with trusted dataset versions and combine automated screening

entries.name: Validate AI Model
entries.description: Evaluate AI models against defined functional requirements before deployment and throughout their operational lifecycle. Validate newly trained or acquired models and repeat evaluation after fine-tuning, model updates, or changes to the conditions in which the model is used. Use representative evaluation data and adversarial test cases appropriate to the model's capabilities and intended use. Test for unexpected behavior associated with poisoned training data, model tampering, backdoor triggers, adversarial inputs, and sensitive information disclosure. For generative models, include evaluation

entries.name: Predictive AI Multi-Sensor Fusion
entries.description: Use independent physical sensors (ideally across multiple modalities or from several perspectives) to avoid relying on a single sensor that may be manipulated, obstructed, or disrupted by an adversary. Relevant sensors may include visible-light cameras, infrared cameras, depth sensors, radar, lidar, microphones, or other physical sensing systems. Corroborate observations across sensors so manipulation of one input source does not overly influence the model's predictions.

entries.name: Predictive AI Input Restoration
entries.description: Preprocess predictive AI inference inputs to remove, reduce, or disrupt adversarial perturbations before the inputs are evaluated by the model. Restoration methods may include denoising, compression, reconstruction, resampling, feature squeezing, randomized transformations, or other modality-appropriate preprocessing. Evaluate restoration methods against adaptive adversaries that account for the preprocessing operation.

entries.name: Restrict Library Loading
entries.description: Prevent abuse of library loading mechanisms in the operating system and software to load untrusted code by configuring appropriate library loading mechanisms and investigating potential vulnerable software. File formats such as pickle files that are commonly used to store AI models can contain exploits that allow for loading of malicious libraries.

entries.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
entries.description: Encrypt sensitive data such as AI models to protect against adversaries attempting to access sensitive data.

entries.name: Code Signing
entries.description: Enforce binary and application integrity with digital signature verification to prevent untrusted code from executing. Adversaries can embed malicious code in AI software or models. Developers should also cryptographically sign SBOM and AIBOM components that track model or data provenance. Enforcement of code signing can prevent the compromise of the AI supply chain and prevent execution of malicious code.

entries.name: Verify AI Artifacts
entries.description: Verify the integrity and authenticity of AI artifacts before importing, loading, or deploying them. Artifacts may include model weights and checkpoints, datasets, tokenizers, model configurations, prompt templates, and agent configuration files. Verify the complete set of files used by the AI system, including supporting files that can alter model or agent behavior. Compare cryptographic hashes against expected values obtained from an authenticated publisher. Where digital signatures or signed manifests are available, verify that they cover the artifacts being used and were produced by an auth

entries.name: Predictive AI Adversarial Input Detection
entries.description: Detect and block digital or physical adversarial examples submitted to predictive AI models. Adversarial examples are inputs modified or constructed to cause misclassification, missed detection, excessive computation, or another attacker-selected behavior. Apply detection before model inference and monitor for input characteristics or query patterns associated with adversarial example generation, transfer attacks, or black-box optimization. Detection may use statistical tests, auxiliary models, consistency checks, input distribution analysis, or modality-specific adversarial example detectors.

entries.name: Vulnerability Scanning
entries.description: Vulnerability scanning is used to find potentially exploitable software vulnerabilities to remediate them. File formats such as pickle files that are commonly used to store AI models can contain exploits that allow for arbitrary code execution. These files should be scanned for potentially unsafe calls, which could be used to execute code, create new processes, or establish networking capabilities. Adversaries may embed malicious code in corrupt model files, so scanners should be capable of working with models that cannot be fully de-serialized. Model artifacts, downstream products produced by

entries.name: AI Model Distribution Methods
entries.description: Deploying AI models to edge devices can increase the attack surface of the system. Consider serving models in the cloud to reduce the level of access the adversary has to the model. Also consider computing features in the cloud to prevent gray-box attacks, where an adversary has access to the model preprocessing methods.

entries.name: User Training
entries.description: Educate AI model developers to on AI supply chain risks and potentially malicious AI artifacts. Educate users on how to identify deepfakes and phishing attempts.

entries.name: Control Access to AI Models and Data in Production
entries.description: Require users to verify their identities before accessing a production model. Require authentication for API endpoints and monitor production model queries to ensure compliance with usage policies and to prevent model misuse.

entries.name: Generative AI Guardrails
entries.description: Guardrails are safety controls placed between users, tools, and generative AI models to evaluate prompts, retrieved context, model outputs, and agent actions before they are accepted, executed, or shown to a user. They can help block, modify, or route unwanted content such as malicious code, malicious instructions, sensitive data, unsupported claims, policy-violating responses, or unsafe tool requests.
